scope: Proposition C.3 of the manuscript “Conditional good minimal models for compact Kähler fourfolds” (preprints/Conditional-good-minimal-models-for-compact-Kahler-fourfolds-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 034 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 eebddaadef6935c3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 95. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Choose ℓ divisible by m and every nonzero integer |mai|, and set a = ℓ/m. There is a normal tame Deligne–Mumford stack X, considered on a neighborhood of a reduced Cartier divisor S of pure dimension N = n − 1, together with a morphism to X and a reduced boundary T having no component in common with S, with the following properties. (i) The pair (X, S + T) is log canonical, and a fixed isomorphism of reflexive sheaves is given by ωX (S + T) ≃ OX (aS). (∗adj) The support of T is locally set-theoretically principal. The ambient space and S are Cohen– Macaulay on scheme charts. Off T, the ambient space is Gorenstein and the displayed isomorphism is ordinary Cartier adjunction data. (ii) Put J = (S ∩ T)red. Both S and J are Du Bois on scheme charts, the ideal IJ/S is maximal Cohen–Macaulay, and B := HomS(IJ/S, ωS) ≃ OS(aS). The identification agrees off J with the residue convention specified by (∗adj). (iii) There is a finite representable morphism S −→ D ×P P whose image covers Supp G+. The line OS(S) is the pullback of C. The image of J in P has dimension less than r, whereas the image of S has dimension r. (iv) There is a smooth projective bundle p : Y → P and a representable projective morphism g : S → Y. Writing h = p ◦ g and T = SpecP h∗OS, the morphism g factors through a closed embedding T ,→ Y, and g∗OS = OT , OS(S) = g∗ C, B = g∗ Ca . (v) For a separated quasi-projective scheme chart U → Y that is etale and of finite type, put SU = S ×Y U. The etale morphism SU → S extends compatibly to every nilpotent thickening qS in X. The resulting qSU are quasi-projective schemes, separated and quasi-finite over X. All the adjunction and duality identifications are compatible with changes of etale chart.
